items.title: EC considering EU strategic gas reserve: deputy director-general
points: The European Commission is considering whether to push for an EU-specific strategic natural gas reserve, Deputy Director-General for Energy Mechthild Wörsdörfer told Platts.
“We haven’t decided yet if we come out with an EU strategic gas reserve or not,” Wörsdörfer said, speaking on the sidelines of the Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation meeting in Warsaw.
While routine storage is a cornerstone of the EU system, member states have increasingly eyed specialized strategic reserves to weather acute emergencies.
Two major EU gas hubs — Germany and the Netherlands — have recently rolled out plans for their own such reserves domestically.
Both are relatively limited: Amsterdam’s is set at 5 terawatt-hour (473 million cubic meters) while Berlin’s is 24 TWh.
These represent some 3.5% and 9.7% of each country’s gas storage capacity, respectively, according to data from Gas Infrastructure Europe.
The Dutch government has said it would look into expanding its reserve if the EU lets existing gas storage requirements phase out after next year.

items.title: European Natural Gas Prices Rise Further
points: European natural gas prices rose above €86/MWh on Friday, extending gains from the previous session amid concerns about tighter winter supplies.
Lower Norwegian gas exports, partly due to an outage at the Troll gas field, added pressure to an already constrained market.
Meanwhile, forecasts of colder temperatures across Northwest Europe point to stronger heating demand and faster withdrawals from storage.

European gas storage remains relatively low at 69.8% full as of November 19, compared with 81.2% a year earlier, leaving the region with a thinner supply cushion and greater exposure to price spikes during periods of extreme cold.

The Middle East war has heavily strained Europe’s gas supply, with persistent tensions and continued attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz threatening prolonged disruptions to LNG shipments from the region.

points: Offshore construction contractor Seaway 7 is preparing to deploy three vessels on SSE Renewables’ proposed 1.4GW Berwick Bank B offshore wind development in Scotland.

The vessels form part of Seaway 7’s proposed engineering, procurement, construction and installation package covering turbine foundations and inter-array cables.

points: Nearly three years after the Navy relaxed its dress code to permit Indian attire in officers’ messes, the option has found few, if any, takers, officials aware of the matter said on Friday.
The change was introduced in February 2024 when Admiral R Hari Kumar was at the Navy’s helm, amid a broader push to indigenise the service’s traditions and practices.
“The traditional ensemble of kurta-pyjamas and sleeveless jackets with formal shoes or closed sandals has barely made an appearance in Navy officers’ messes.

Several officers said they had not seen Indian attire at mess gatherings, except in a March 2024 photograph featuring Admiral Hari Kumar, his successor and the most recently retired Navy chief Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi, along with other senior officers.
As part of its push to shed colonial-era practices, the Navy adopted a new ensign, did away with batons for commanders and allowed officers to wear Indian attire in messes.
The rank revamp would have covered more than 65,000 sailors.

items.title: 7-week-old elephant calf Raja, born with fractured leg, air-lifted to Vantara for treatment
points: A seven-week-old elephant calf suffering from a fractured thigh bone and multiple health complications, is being airlifted from Assam to Vantara in Gujarat's Jamnagar for specialised treatment.
The airlift, being facilitated by Vantara founder Anant Ambani, will be the third such operation in India, according to a release issued by the wildlife care facility on Friday.
The elephant calf, named Raja, was born last month in Gogamukh, Assam, and sustained a fracture in his right hind leg shortly after birth.
Transporting the calf by road would have involved travel of over 2,500 km, and could have posed additional risks to his already fragile health condition.
According to Vantara, Raja's 11-year-old mother was young and inexperienced while giving birth.
Vantara's Rapid Response Team reached Raja on October 8, nearly a week after his birth, after the elephant calf's caretakers sought assistance.
On October 10, Raja was oved to his owner's residence, where the Vantara team continued his treatment and monitoring.

items.title: India Inc. posts strongest earnings quarter since late 2023, full-year growth seen at 14%
points: Indian corporate earnings delivered a strong second quarter of FY27, with net income rising 19 per cent year-on-year, excluding commodities, marking the best quarterly performance since December 2023, according to an HSBC Global Investment Research report.
Around 67 per cent of companies in HSBC’s India coverage universe reported results at or above consensus expectations.
Sales grew 17 per cent year-on-year on an ex-commodities basis, with growth broadening across sectors and market capitalisations.
Mid- and small-cap companies led with earnings growth of 30 per cent and 32 per cent, respectively, though large-cap performance also improved meaningfully during the quarter.
For the full year FY27, consensus forecasts net income growth of approximately 14 per cent, reflecting an expected moderation from 16 per cent in the first half to 12 per cent in the second half.
Since end-September, FY27 earnings estimates have been revised upward by roughly 1.5 percentage points, with upgrades covering around 40 per cent of companies.

points: The Supreme Court on Friday allowed the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp atop Thiruparankundram hill on November 24 as a one-time measure.

items.title: Terms of Trade: Poverty is dead, long-live anti-poverty programmes
points: The latest numbers show that poverty, or the share of population living below $3 in 2021 purchasing power parity (PPP) terms, fell to just 2.6% in 2023.

items.title: India scraps compulsory retirement age for ships
points: India has scrapped compulsory retirement ages for ships flying its flag, reversing a policy designed to push older tonnage out of the country’s merchant fleet.

The Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) issued a new order this week 18 allowing existing Indian-flagged vessels to continue trading regardless of age, provided they meet prescribed technical and safety standards.
Tankers, bulk carriers and general cargo ships over 20 years old can now be considered for registration, subject to a technical review and approval process.
For containerships, gas carriers and chemical tankers, the corresponding threshold is 25 years.
Ships below those limits remain subject to graduated inspection and classification requirements depending on their age.
The latest move overturns restrictions introduced in 2023 and revised in January this year, which had imposed firm age limits on ships entering and remaining in the Indian fleet.
